sentences.text: The name Orkoraptor translates to "Toothed River thief," derived from the Aoniken word "Orr-Korr," which is the local name for the La Leona River.
This medium-sized theropod measured 8.4 meters in length and weighed 1400 kilograms.
Its skull featured specialized teeth that were unserrated on the front side and possessed an 8-shaped cross section.
Found in southern Patagonia, Argentina, Orkoraptor is one of the most southerly known carnivorous dinosaurs in South America.
The genus was described by Novas, Ezcurra, and Lecuona in 2008, based on the holotype specimen MPM-Pv 3457, which was excavated in 2001.
Original describers could not conclusively assign Orkoraptor to a specific family because many features contradicted those of coelurosaurs.
Subsequent studies recovered Orkoraptor within the clade Megaraptora.

Phylogenetic trees from the Gualicho shinyae publication suggest megaraptorans are either allosauroids or basal coelurosaurs, leading a 2009 study by Benson, Carrano, and Brusatte to classify Orkoraptor as an allosauroid within the family Neovenatoridae.
Orkoraptor lived during the late Cretaceous Period in Argentina.
While originally thought to be from the Maastrichtian, the time range is now estimated from 83.6 to 72.2 million years ago, spanning the Cenomanian to Santonian and Campanian to Maastrichtian epochs.
